properties.natural_language: Before Compute Valid Jump Destinations can execute, the system must be in Contract Bytecode Loaded.
After Compute Valid Jump Destinations completes, Check Code Bounds must proceed as specified by: For each potential destination, check bounds.
After Check Code Bounds completes, Check JUMPDEST Opcode must proceed as specified by: Bounds valid, check opcode.
After Check JUMPDEST Opcode completes, Check Not Within PUSH Data must proceed as specified by: Is JUMPDEST, verify not in PUSH data.
After Check Not Within PUSH Data completes, the system must transition to Valid Jump Set Computed with all state invariants preserved.
After Valid Jump Set Computed completes, Jump Destination Valid must proceed as specified by: Destination in valid set.
After Valid Jump Set Computed completes, Jump Destination Invalid must proceed as specified by: Destination not in valid set.
Before Pop Destination from Stack can execute, the system must be in JUMP/JUMPI Instruction Executed.
After Pop Destination from Stack completes, Validate Jump Destination must proceed as specified by: Check destination validity.
After Validate Jump Destination completes, the system must transition to Jump Allowed with all state invariants preserved.
After Validate Jump Destination completes, the system must transition to Execution Halted: Invalid Jump with all state invariants preserved.
Before Update Program Counter can execute, the system must be in Jump Allowed.
After Update Program Counter completes, the system must transition to Execution Continues at New PC with all state invariants preserved.
Before Read Opcode at Position can execute, the system must be in Bytecode Iteration Started.
After Read Opcode at Position completes, Detect PUSH-N Instruction must proceed as specified by: Check if PUSH instruction.
After Detect PUSH-N Instruction completes, Calculate Data Payload Size must proceed as specified by: Is PUSH, calculate data size.
After Calculate Data Payload Size completes, Mark Data Range as Invalid must proceed as specified by: Mark following bytes as data.
After Mark Data Range as Invalid completes, the system must transition to Data Range Marked with all state invariants preserved.
Before Skip to Next Instruction can execute, the system must be in Data Range Marked.
After Skip to Next Instruction completes, Read Opcode at Position must proceed as specified by: Process next opcode.
After Detect PUSH-N Instruction completes, Read Opcode at Position must proceed as specified by: Not PUSH, advance by 1.
After Read Opcode at Position completes, the system must transition to Bytecode Iteration Complete with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-CANCUN-RUNTIME-01): The documentation only covers get_valid_jump_destinations() but does not document other runtime functions like message call processing or contract creation. — the system must enforce: Assume other runtime functions follow standard EVM semantics as defined in the Yellow Paper and prior fork specifications.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-CANCUN-RUNTIME-02): The handling of 'invalid opcodes' during bytecode iteration is mentioned but not fully specified. — the system must enforce: Assume invalid opcodes are treated as single-byte instructions for iteration purposes, not causing analysis failure.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-CANCUN-RUNTIME-03): The behavior when PUSH data extends beyond bytecode bounds is not explicitly defined. — the system must enforce: Assume PUSH instructions at the end of bytecode that would reference out-of-bounds data are still valid but push zero-padded values during execution.

The system assumes: Pre-computing valid jump destinations prevents attackers from jumping into PUSH data to execute arbitrary byte sequences as opcodes.. If violated: Arbitrary code execution within contracts, potentially bypassing security checks or accessing unauthorized functionality.

The system assumes: Jump destination analysis is performed once per contract call and cached for the duration of execution.. If violated: Re-computing on every JUMP would cause significant performance overhead, potentially enabling gas-based DoS attacks.

The system assumes: The JUMPDEST opcode (0x5B) is reserved and cannot appear naturally in contract execution except as a valid jump target.. If violated: If 0x5B could be interpreted differently in certain contexts, jump validation could be bypassed.

The system assumes: Contract bytecode is immutable after deployment, so valid jump destinations cannot change.. If violated: Mutable bytecode would require re-analysis of jump destinations, introducing security and performance concerns.

All data received via Begin block processing from EXT-VALIDATOR-PROPOSER-P2P must be validated before processing. Block must pass signature verification, slot validation, parent existence check, and state transition validation before being accepted into fork choice. Equivocating proposers must be detected.
If input from EXT-VALIDATOR-PROPOSER-P2P via Begin block processing fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.

All data received via Execution envelope received from EXT-EL-VIA-ENGINE-API must be validated before processing. Execution payload envelope must be verified for data availability (blob KZG commitments). JWT authentication validates the channel but payload content integrity must be checked independently. Payload must correspond to a known block.
If input from EXT-EL-VIA-ENGINE-API via Execution envelope received fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
After Process on_block completes, the system must transition to Payload Status Pending with all state invariants preserved.
After Payload Status Pending completes, Payload Status Empty must proceed as specified by: Payload not received within deadline.
After Process on_execution_payload completes, the system must transition to Payload Status Full with all state invariants preserved.
Before Compute Fork Choice Head can execute, the system must be in Payload Status Full.
Before Compute Fork Choice Head can execute, the system must be in Payload Status Empty.

All data received via PTC member submits payload attestation from EXT-PTC-VALIDATOR-P2P must be validated before processing. PTC attestations must verify: validator is in assigned PTC committee for the slot, attestation signature is valid, and validator index maps correctly to ptc_vote boolean vector. Quorum threshold (>256/512) required before payload timeliness is accepted.
If input from EXT-PTC-VALIDATOR-P2P via PTC member submits payload attestation fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
After Process on_payload_attestation_message completes, Check Payload Timeliness must proceed as specified by: Evaluate accumulated votes.
After Check Payload Timeliness completes, the system must transition to PTC Quorum Reached with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Payload Timeliness completes, the system must transition to PTC Quorum Not Reached with all state invariants preserved.
Before Apply Payload Status Tiebreaker can execute, the system must be in PTC Quorum Reached.
Before Check Parent Block Slot can execute, the system must be in Block Proposed in Current Slot.
After Check Parent Block Slot completes, the system must transition to Proposer Boost Applied with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Parent Block Slot completes, Check Weight Threshold must proceed as specified by: Parent from previous slot.
After Check Weight Threshold completes, Check for Early Equivocations must proceed as specified by: Weight threshold met.
After Check Weight Threshold completes, the system must transition to Proposer Boost Denied with all state invariants preserved.
After Check for Early Equivocations completes, the system must transition to Proposer Boost Applied with all state invariants preserved.
After Check for Early Equivocations completes, the system must transition to Proposer Boost Denied with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-GLOAS-FC-01): The term 'sufficient weight threshold' for proposer boost conditions is not precisely quantified in the fork choice description. — the system must enforce: Assume the weight threshold follows the existing proposer boost percentage from the base fork choice specification (e.g., 40% committee weight). This needs verification against the full Gloas spec.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-GLOAS-FC-02): The specification mentions 'early equivocations' without defining the precise time boundary between early and late equivocations. — the system must enforce: Assume 'early' refers to equivocations detected before the attestation deadline within the slot. This aligns with the timeliness index structure.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-GLOAS-FC-03): The behavior when on_block constructs parent state and the parent has both execution_payload_states and block_states entries is not fully specified for edge cases. — the system must enforce: Assume execution_payload_states takes priority over block_states when both exist for the same parent block hash, as FULL state subsumes EMPTY state.

The system assumes: PTC committee members are assumed to honestly report payload presence based on their actual observation.. If violated: A colluding PTC majority (>256 of 512) could falsely attest to payload presence or absence, manipulating fork choice between FULL and EMPTY tracks.

The system assumes: An attacker cannot control a majority of PTC committee validators for a given slot.. If violated: Attacker could force the chain to follow the EMPTY track even when payloads are available, or force FULL track for unavailable payloads.

The system assumes: The execution payload envelope arrives within the PTC deadline for honest proposers.. If violated: Honest proposers' blocks may be penalized to EMPTY status due to network delays, giving an advantage to well-connected attackers.

The system assumes: The slot-based latest message tracking (replacing epoch-based) does not introduce additional memory or computational overhead that could be exploited.. If violated: Potential denial-of-service if tracking per-slot messages significantly increases state size, especially over long non-finality periods.
Before Decode BLOBBASEFEE Opcode can execute, the system must be in EVM Executing Bytecode.
After Decode BLOBBASEFEE Opcode completes, Read Blob Gas Price from Header must proceed as specified by: Read blob gas price from header.
After Read Blob Gas Price from Header completes, the system must transition to Blob Base Fee Retrieved with all state invariants preserved.
Before Push Value to Stack can execute, the system must be in Blob Base Fee Retrieved.
After Push Value to Stack completes, the system must transition to Blob Base Fee on Stack with all state invariants preserved.
Before Deduct Gas Cost can execute, the system must be in Blob Base Fee on Stack.
After Deduct Gas Cost completes, the system must transition to Gas Deducted with all state invariants preserved.
Before Compute Gas Cost can execute, the system must be in BLOBBASEFEE Opcode Invoked.
After Compute Gas Cost completes, the system must transition to Gas Cost Determined with all state invariants preserved.
Before Check Remaining Gas can execute, the system must be in Gas Cost Determined.
After Check Remaining Gas completes, the system must transition to Gas Sufficient with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Remaining Gas completes, the system must transition to Out of Gas with all state invariants preserved.
Before Query Current Blob Base Fee can execute, the system must be in Rollup Contract Executing.
After Query Current Blob Base Fee completes, the system must transition to Blob Fee Known to Contract with all state invariants preserved.
Before Compute Blob Data Cost can execute, the system must be in Blob Fee Known to Contract.
After Compute Blob Data Cost completes, the system must transition to Blob Data Cost Computed with all state invariants preserved.
Before Adjust User Fees can execute, the system must be in Blob Data Cost Computed.
After Adjust User Fees completes, the system must transition to User Fees Adjusted with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP7516-01): The specification does not define behavior when BLOBBASEFEE is called on a chain without EIP-4844 enabled or before the fork activation. — the system must enforce: Assume BLOBBASEFEE is an invalid opcode on chains/blocks without EIP-4844, causing execution to revert with invalid opcode error.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP7516-02): The reference to 'get_blob_gasprice(header)' assumes familiarity with EIP-4844 but doesn't specify behavior if blob gas fields are missing. — the system must enforce: Assume the opcode is only valid after EIP-4844 activation when blob gas fields are guaranteed present in headers.

The system assumes: EIP-4844 is active and blob gas price is available in the block header before BLOBBASEFEE can be used.. If violated: Contracts calling BLOBBASEFEE on pre-4844 blocks would fail or return undefined values.

The system assumes: The blob base fee value in the header accurately reflects the actual blob gas market conditions.. If violated: If blob base fee can be manipulated, rollup contracts may under/over-charge users for data availability.

The system assumes: The 2 gas cost is sufficient to prevent spam while remaining affordable for legitimate use cases.. If violated: If cost is too low, BLOBBASEFEE could be used in gas-cost attacks; if too high, it limits utility for cost tracking.
Before Push Value onto Stack can execute, the system must be in Stack Ready for Operation.
Before Pop Value from Stack can execute, the system must be in Stack Ready for Operation.
After Push Value onto Stack completes, the system must transition to Stack Modified with all state invariants preserved.
After Pop Value from Stack completes, the system must transition to Stack Modified with all state invariants preserved.
After Pop Value from Stack completes, the system must transition to Value Returned from Pop with all state invariants preserved.
Before Check Stack Size can execute, the system must be in Push Operation Requested.
After Check Stack Size completes, the system must transition to Stack Has Space with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Stack Size completes, the system must transition to Stack Full (1024 elements) with all state invariants preserved.
Before Raise StackOverflowError can execute, the system must be in Stack Full (1024 elements).
After Raise StackOverflowError completes, the system must transition to Stack Overflow Error State with all state invariants preserved.
Before Perform Push can execute, the system must be in Stack Has Space.
After Perform Push completes, the system must transition to Push Complete with all state invariants preserved.
Before Check Stack Empty can execute, the system must be in Pop Operation Requested.
After Check Stack Empty completes, the system must transition to Stack Has Elements with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Stack Empty completes, the system must transition to Stack Empty (0 elements) with all state invariants preserved.
Before Raise StackUnderflowError can execute, the system must be in Stack Empty (0 elements).
After Raise StackUnderflowError completes, the system must transition to Stack Underflow Error State with all state invariants preserved.
Before Perform Pop can execute, the system must be in Stack Has Elements.
After Perform Pop completes, the system must transition to Pop Complete with all state invariants preserved.
Before Validate Input Count can execute, the system must be in Opcode Received for Execution.
After Validate Input Count completes, Validate Output Space must proceed as specified by: Inputs OK, check outputs.
After Validate Output Space completes, the system must transition to Stack Validation Passed with all state invariants preserved.
After Validate Input Count completes, the system must transition to Stack Validation Failed with all state invariants preserved.
After Validate Output Space completes, the system must transition to Stack Validation Failed with all state invariants preserved.
Before Execute Opcode can execute, the system must be in Stack Validation Passed.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-CANCUN-STACK-01): The specification does not detail stack behavior for DUP and SWAP operations beyond basic push/pop. — the system must enforce: Assume DUP and SWAP use peek operations or multiple pop/push sequences. These must respect the same 1024 limit and underflow checks.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-CANCUN-STACK-02): Error handling behavior after StackOverflowError or StackUnderflowError is not fully specified. — the system must enforce: Assume these errors cause immediate execution halt with all gas consumed, consistent with other EVM execution errors.
The system assumes: The underlying Python list implementation handles append/pop operations atomically.. If violated: Race conditions could corrupt stack state in concurrent execution scenarios.
The system assumes: Attackers cannot bypass stack bounds checks through any combination of opcodes.. If violated: Stack corruption could enable arbitrary code execution or state manipulation.
The system assumes: All U256 values can be safely stored and retrieved from the stack without loss.. If violated: Value truncation or corruption would break contract execution correctness.

The system assumes: The 1024 stack limit is sufficient for all legitimate smart contract execution patterns.. If violated: Legitimate contracts could fail unexpectedly, but this is a design choice not a bug.

All data received via User submits contract creation transaction from EXT-CONTRACT-DEPLOYER-TX must be validated before processing. Full transaction validation required: signature verification, nonce check, gas limit validation, init code execution, and returned bytecode size check (<=24576 bytes per EIP-170). Out-of-gas on size violation.
If input from EXT-CONTRACT-DEPLOYER-TX via User submits contract creation transaction fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
Before Execute Initialization Code can execute, the system must be in Contract Creation Started.
After Execute Initialization Code completes, the system must transition to Init Code Execution Complete with all state invariants preserved.
Before Check Code Size Limit can execute, the system must be in Init Code Execution Complete.
After Check Code Size Limit completes, the system must transition to Size Within Limit with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Code Size Limit completes, the system must transition to Size Exceeds Limit with all state invariants preserved.
Before Deploy Contract can execute, the system must be in Size Within Limit.
After Deploy Contract completes, the system must transition to Contract Deployed with all state invariants preserved.
Before Trigger Out-of-Gas can execute, the system must be in Size Exceeds Limit.
After Trigger Out-of-Gas completes, the system must transition to Contract Creation Failed with all state invariants preserved.
Before Measure Code Length can execute, the system must be in Bytecode Returned from Init.
After Measure Code Length completes, Compare to MAX_CODE_SIZE must proceed as specified by: Compare measured length.
After Compare to MAX_CODE_SIZE completes, the system must transition to Valid Size with all state invariants preserved.
After Compare to MAX_CODE_SIZE completes, the system must transition to Invalid Size with all state invariants preserved.
After Gas Remaining After Init completes, Size Limit Violated must proceed as specified by: Size check fails.
Before Consume All Remaining Gas can execute, the system must be in Size Limit Violated.
After Consume All Remaining Gas completes, the system must transition to Gas Exhausted with all state invariants preserved.
After Gas Exhausted completes, No Gas Refund must proceed as specified by: No refund issued.

All data received via Receive block from network from EXT-VALIDATOR-PROPOSER-P2P must be validated before processing. Block must pass signature verification, slot validation, parent existence check, and state transition validation before being accepted into fork choice. Equivocating proposers must be detected.
If input from EXT-VALIDATOR-PROPOSER-P2P via Receive block from network fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
Before Verify Contract Creations can execute, the system must be in Block Validation in Progress.
After Verify Contract Creations completes, the system must transition to Bounded Verification Time with all state invariants preserved.
After Bounded Verification Time completes, DoS Attack Prevented must proceed as specified by: Verification completes in bounded time.
While in Unbounded Verification (Pre-EIP170): Without size limits, attackers could deploy massive contracts.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP170-01): The specification uses 'more than' MAX_CODE_SIZE, implying contracts of exactly 24576 bytes are valid, but this boundary case could be clearer. — the system must enforce: Confirm that code length <= 24576 is valid, and code length > 24576 triggers failure (strict inequality).

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP170-02): The specification does not address what happens if the init code itself exceeds the size limit during deployment. — the system must enforce: Assume the limit applies only to the returned deployment bytecode, not the init code.
The system assumes: The MAX_CODE_SIZE limit is applied consistently across all client implementations.. If violated: Consensus failures if clients disagree on valid contract sizes.
The system assumes: 24576 bytes is sufficient for most legitimate contract use cases.. If violated: Developers may need to use proxy patterns or contract splitting, increasing complexity.

The system assumes: Without size limits, an attacker could deploy contracts large enough to cause DoS conditions.. If violated: If there are other limiting factors (gas cost), the attack may not be practical anyway.
The system assumes: Block producers will not include invalid transactions that exceed size limits.. If violated: Invalid blocks would be rejected by validating nodes, causing network churn.
Before Check Petersburg Activation Block can execute, the system must be in Pre-Petersburg Consensus Rules.
After Check Petersburg Activation Block completes, the system must transition to Petersburg Rules Active with all state invariants preserved.
Before Disable EIP-1283 SSTORE Metering can execute, the system must be in Petersburg Rules Active.
After Disable EIP-1283 SSTORE Metering completes, the system must transition to EIP-1283 Disabled with all state invariants preserved.
Before Compare Fork Activation Blocks can execute, the system must be in Fork Activation Blocks Configured.
After Compare Fork Activation Blocks completes, the system must transition to Same Block Activation Detected with all state invariants preserved.
Before Apply Petersburg Precedence can execute, the system must be in Same Block Activation Detected.
After Apply Petersburg Precedence completes, the system must transition to Constantinople Without EIP-1283 with all state invariants preserved.
After EIP-1283 Net Gas Metering Active completes, Reentrancy Attack Vector Present must proceed as specified by: Cheap SSTORE enables attack.
Before Evaluate Security Risk can execute, the system must be in Reentrancy Attack Vector Present.
After Evaluate Security Risk completes, Revert SSTORE Gas Pricing must proceed as specified by: Decision to revert.
After Revert SSTORE Gas Pricing completes, the system must transition to Reentrancy Vector Eliminated with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP1716-01): The specific reentrancy attack vector that necessitated EIP-1283 removal is not detailed in this EIP. — the system must enforce: Assume the attack involves contracts that relied on transfer gas stipends being insufficient for storage writes, which EIP-1283 would have violated. Consult EIP-1283 security analysis for details.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP1716-02): The meaning of 'Petersburg takes priority' when forks activate at same block is implied but not formally specified. — the system must enforce: Assume Petersburg is processed after Constantinople in the fork ordering, effectively overriding EIP-1283 inclusion.

The system assumes: All client implementations will correctly implement the fork precedence logic when Petersburg and Constantinople share the same activation block.. If violated: Consensus split between clients that enable vs disable EIP-1283, leading to chain fork.
The system assumes: Node operators will upgrade to Petersburg-aware clients before block 7,280,000.. If violated: Non-upgraded nodes will fork off on a separate chain with EIP-1283 enabled.

All data received via Node returns QUANTITY value from EXT-ETHEREUM-NODE-BACKEND must be validated before processing. Provider should validate response format. Connection should be over secure transport. Timeouts must be implemented.
If input from EXT-ETHEREUM-NODE-BACKEND via Node returns QUANTITY value fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
Data from external entity EXT-RPC-NODE via Node returns null must be treated as untrusted and validated.
Before Send eth_txGasLimitCap Request can execute, the system must be in Client Needs Gas Cap Info.
After Send eth_txGasLimitCap Request completes, the system must transition to Awaiting Node Response with all state invariants preserved.
Before Node Computes Effective Cap can execute, the system must be in Awaiting Node Response.
Before Compute Minimum of Caps can execute, the system must be in Protocol Cap Defined.
Before Compute Minimum of Caps can execute, the system must be in Policy Cap Configured.
After Compute Minimum of Caps completes, the system must transition to Effective Cap Computed with all state invariants preserved.
Before Return Null can execute, the system must be in No Protocol Cap.
While in No Policy Cap: Node has no local policy cap configured.
Data from external entity EXT-USER via User initiates transaction in wallet must be treated as untrusted and validated.
Before Query Gas Cap can execute, the system must be in Wallet Preparing Transaction.
After Query Gas Cap completes, the system must transition to Gas Cap Known with all state invariants preserved.
Before Estimate Gas Needed can execute, the system must be in Gas Cap Known.
After Estimate Gas Needed completes, Validate Against Cap must proceed as specified by: Compare to cap.
After Validate Against Cap completes, the system must transition to Transaction Within Cap with all state invariants preserved.
After Validate Against Cap completes, the system must transition to Transaction Exceeds Cap with all state invariants preserved.
Before Warn User can execute, the system must be in Transaction Exceeds Cap.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP8123-01): The relationship between protocolCap and policyCap is defined but it's unclear if nodes MUST enforce policyCap at the protocol level or only at mempool admission — the system must enforce: Assume policyCap is only for mempool admission policy, not consensus. Transactions above policyCap but below protocolCap could still be included by other nodes.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP8123-02): The specification does not define behavior when protocol cap changes (e.g., at a hard fork) — the system must enforce: Assume the method returns the current effective cap at query time. Clients should re-query after known hard forks.

The system assumes: The node is trusted to return accurate cap information. If violated: Malicious nodes could return incorrect caps, causing transaction failures or users to believe they can submit transactions that will be rejected

The system assumes: Different chains (Ethereum, Arbitrum, Polygon) have different protocol caps that clients need to discover. If violated: If all chains had the same cap, this method would be unnecessary. The heterogeneous environment motivates this EIP.

The system assumes: Wallets and tools will query this method instead of hardcoding gas limits. If violated: If tools continue to use hardcoded values, they may construct invalid transactions or fail to utilize available gas
Before Create Meta EIP Draft can execute, the system must be in Hard Fork Planning Initiated.
After Create Meta EIP Draft completes, the system must transition to Meta EIP in Draft Status with all state invariants preserved.
Before Freeze Hard Fork Changes can execute, the system must be in Meta EIP in Draft Status.
After Freeze Hard Fork Changes completes, the system must transition to Meta EIP Accepted with all state invariants preserved.
Before Activate Hard Fork on Network can execute, the system must be in Meta EIP Accepted.
After Activate Hard Fork on Network completes, the system must transition to Meta EIP Final with all state invariants preserved.
Before Review in All Core Devs Meeting can execute, the system must be in EIP Proposed for Inclusion.
After Review in All Core Devs Meeting completes, the system must transition to EIP Under Review with all state invariants preserved.
Before Verify Client Implementations can execute, the system must be in EIP Under Review.
After Verify Client Implementations completes, the system must transition to Implementation Missing with all state invariants preserved.
After Verify Client Implementations completes, the system must transition to Implementations Complete with all state invariants preserved.
After Implementation Missing completes, EIP Rejected from Hard Fork must proceed as specified by: Deadline passed without impl.
Before Check for Security Issues can execute, the system must be in Implementations Complete.
After Check for Security Issues completes, the system must transition to Security Issues Identified with all state invariants preserved.
After Check for Security Issues completes, the system must transition to No Security Issues with all state invariants preserved.
After Security Issues Identified completes, EIP Rejected from Hard Fork must proceed as specified by: Security blocks inclusion.
After No Security Issues completes, EIP Accepted for Hard Fork must proceed as specified by: EIP accepted.
Before Deploy to Testnet can execute, the system must be in EIP Accepted for Hard Fork.
After Deploy to Testnet completes, the system must transition to EIP Included (Post-Testnet) with all state invariants preserved.
Before Set Acceptance Deadline can execute, the system must be in Timeline Not Yet Set.
After Set Acceptance Deadline completes, the system must transition to Acceptance Deadline Active with all state invariants preserved.
Before Set Implementation Deadline can execute, the system must be in Acceptance Deadline Active.
After Set Implementation Deadline completes, the system must transition to Implementation Deadline Active with all state invariants preserved.
Before Set Testnet Upgrade Date can execute, the system must be in Implementation Deadline Active.
After Set Testnet Upgrade Date completes, the system must transition to Testnet Date Scheduled with all state invariants preserved.
Before Set Mainnet Activation Block can execute, the system must be in Testnet Date Scheduled.
After Set Mainnet Activation Block completes, the system must transition to Mainnet Activation Scheduled with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP233-01): The term 'major client implementations' is not precisely defined - unclear which clients qualify and what percentage of network hashpower/stake they must represent. — the system must enforce: Assume 'major clients' means at least 3 of the main execution clients (Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon) that together represent >80% of network participation.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP233-02): The process for handling emergency security patches that need rapid deployment is not addressed. — the system must enforce: Assume emergency fixes can bypass the standard timeline through an expedited All Core Devs decision, but this needs separate documentation.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP233-03): The meaning of 'soft deadline' for implementations is unclear - what happens if the deadline is missed? — the system must enforce: Assume soft deadline means the EIP may be excluded from the hard fork if implementations are not ready, but exceptions can be made case-by-case.

The system assumes: The All Core Devs group acts in good faith and makes decisions that benefit the Ethereum network as a whole.. If violated: Malicious or captured governance could lead to inclusion of harmful changes or exclusion of necessary security fixes.

The system assumes: Client teams have sufficient resources to implement approved EIPs within the specified timeline.. If violated: Hard fork delays, rushed implementations, or incomplete testing could introduce bugs or security vulnerabilities.

The system assumes: The majority of the network (miners/validators and users) will upgrade their clients before the activation block.. If violated: Chain split risk if significant portion of network doesn't upgrade, potentially leading to double-spend attacks during the split.
All data received via Client sends eth_getProof request from EXT-USER-JSON-RPC must be validated before processing. All RPC method calls must be validated. Reserved rpc.* namespace must be enforced.
If input from EXT-USER-JSON-RPC via Client sends eth_getProof request fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
Before Resolve Block Identifier can execute, the system must be in eth_getProof Request Received.
After Resolve Block Identifier completes, Get State Root from Block Header must proceed as specified by: Block resolved, get header.
After Get State Root from Block Header completes, Traverse State Trie must proceed as specified by: Begin account proof collection.
After Traverse State Trie completes, Retrieve Account Data must proceed as specified by: Account found, extract data.
After Retrieve Account Data completes, Traverse Storage Trie must proceed as specified by: Process each storage key.
After Traverse Storage Trie completes, the system must transition to Proof Assembled with all state invariants preserved.
Before Serialize JSON Response can execute, the system must be in Proof Assembled.
After Serialize JSON Response completes, the system must transition to Response Sent to Client with all state invariants preserved.
Before Verify Account Proof can execute, the system must be in Proof Data Received.
Before Verify Account Proof can execute, the system must be in Block Header Trusted.
After Verify Account Proof completes, Verify Storage Proof must proceed as specified by: Account valid, verify storage proofs.
After Verify Account Proof completes, Verify Non-Existence must proceed as specified by: Verify non-existent account/value.
After Verify Storage Proof completes, the system must transition to Proof Valid with all state invariants preserved.
After Verify Non-Existence completes, the system must transition to Proof Valid with all state invariants preserved.
After Verify Account Proof completes, the system must transition to Proof Invalid with all state invariants preserved.
After Verify Storage Proof completes, the system must transition to Proof Invalid with all state invariants preserved.

All data received via Receive proof from untrusted source from EXT-CL-SSZ-DATA-SOURCE must be validated before processing. All SSZ deserialization must validate: offset ordering and range, no excess trailing bytes, list capacity limits, union selector bounds (0-127), bitlist sentinel presence. Malformed data must be rejected. Implementations should enforce maximum nesting depth to prevent stack overflow.
If input from EXT-CL-SSZ-DATA-SOURCE via Receive proof from untrusted source fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
Data from external entity EXT-CONSENSUS-LAYER via Obtain trusted header from consensus must be treated as untrusted and validated.
Before Cryptographic Verification can execute, the system must be in Untrusted RPC Response.
Before Cryptographic Verification can execute, the system must be in Trusted Block Header.
After Cryptographic Verification completes, the system must transition to Data Cryptographically Verified with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP1186-01): The specification does not define behavior when the requested block has been pruned. — the system must enforce: Assume RPC returns an error when historical state is unavailable due to pruning.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP1186-02): The phrase 'enough data to verify this fact' for non-existent values is imprecise. — the system must enforce: Assume proof includes all nodes down to the point where path diverges or branch is empty, following standard Merkle-Patricia trie proof semantics.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP1186-03): Maximum number of storage keys that can be requested is not specified. — the system must enforce: Assume implementation-defined limits to prevent DoS, with error returned if exceeded.

The system assumes: The verifier has access to a trusted block header from a reliable source.. If violated: Verification against a false stateRoot could accept fraudulent proofs, leading to incorrect state assumptions.

The system assumes: An attacker cannot forge Merkle proofs that validate against the correct stateRoot.. If violated: State spoofing would be possible, breaking Layer 2 bridges and light client security.

The system assumes: The RPC endpoint has access to the full state trie for the requested block.. If violated: Incomplete proofs or errors returned, degrading service availability for historical queries.

All data received via EVM CALL to precompile 0x8 from EXT-EVM-CALLER-CONTRACT must be validated before processing. Input must be validated: length divisible by 192, G1 coordinates < p and on curve (or zero point), G2 coordinates valid in F_p² with correct subgroup order q. Gas cost (80000*k + 100000) must be pre-deducted. Invalid input must revert consuming all gas.
If input from EXT-EVM-CALLER-CONTRACT via EVM CALL to precompile 0x8 fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.

After Validate Input Length completes, the system must transition to Input Length Valid with all state invariants preserved.

After Check Product Equals Identity completes, the system must transition to Pairing Verification Failed with all state invariants preserved.

After Count Point Pairs completes, Compute Gas Cost must proceed as specified by: Use k in formula.
After Compute Gas Cost completes, Deduct Gas From Caller must proceed as specified by: Attempt gas deduction.
After Deduct Gas From Caller completes, the system must transition to Insufficient Gas with all state invariants preserved.
After Deduct Gas From Caller completes, the system must transition to Gas Successfully Deducted with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP197-01): The specification states G2 points must have 'order equal to q' but doesn't specify how implementations should verify this efficiently. — the system must enforce: Assume implementations use cofactor multiplication or subgroup membership checks. Verification method should be explicitly specified for security.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP197-02): The behavior when input contains the point at infinity mixed with regular points is not explicitly detailed. — the system must enforce: Assume point at infinity (0,0) encoding is valid for G1 and treated as the identity element in pairing computation. Pairing with infinity should yield 1 in target field.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP197-03): The terms 'fails' and 'reverts' are used - unclear if this means return empty/zero or actual EVM revert. — the system must enforce: Assume 'fails' means the precompile reverts (consumes all gas, returns nothing), consistent with other precompile behavior on invalid input.

The system assumes: The implementation of the optimal ate pairing is mathematically correct and matches the specification's algebraic definition.. If violated: Incorrect pairing implementation could allow invalid zkSNARK proofs to verify, breaking zero-knowledge proof systems.

The system assumes: An attacker cannot find points that pass encoding validation but have incorrect subgroup membership.. If violated: Subgroup attacks could allow forged pairing results, compromising cryptographic protocols built on this precompile.

The system assumes: The alt_bn128 curve parameters (p, q, generators) are correctly hardcoded in all client implementations.. If violated: Parameter mismatches between clients could cause consensus failures or invalid proof acceptance.
